description: Two envelope generators copied from the S-SMP chip of the Super Nintendo, each with a normal and an inverted output

params.text: Sets the height and the polarity of that envelope, -128 to 127; below zero the whole envelope is turned upside down
Sets how long that envelope takes to climb to its full height, 0 to 15, with 15 the slowest and 0 instant
Sets how long that envelope takes to fall from its peak to the sustain level, 0 to 7, with 7 the slowest
Sets the level that envelope falls to before the sustain stage begins, 0 to 7, in eighths of full height
Sets how quickly that envelope keeps falling once it has reached the sustain level, 0 to 31; at the top of the slider it holds indefinitely

inputs.text: Starts that envelope on each rise past 2V and releases it once it falls back to 0V
Restarts that envelope from its attack stage on each rise past 2V, without the gate having to fall first

outputs.text: Carries that envelope, up to 10V at full height
Carries that envelope turned upside down, which is what you patch to duck something rather than open it

notes: neither envelope moves until a gate above 2V reaches its GATE jack, so with nothing patched the module puts out 0V
there is no release control. When the gate falls the chip runs its own very short release, which exists to stop the note clicking, and that stage cannot be adjusted
the panel prints RR over the fifth slider and the manual calls it Release Rate, but the code drives the chip's sustain rate, which sets how fast the envelope falls while the gate is held
